payload.name: Preserve directly-stated facts during extraction
payload.description: When a speaker directly answers a factual question (e.g., how they met, when, where), extract that specific fact as its own memory candidate during extraction instead of only creating a high-level conversation summary.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a direct answer to a factual question (how, when, where, how long), create a separate candidate that captures the specific fact exactly, in addition to any broader conversation summary.
Do not replace an explicit fact with a generic paraphrase (e.g., 'shared experiences about her relationship'); preserve the concrete detail so it remains retrievable later.

solves: Diagnosed cause: extraction summarized the conversation and lost an explicitly stated fact (how a couple met). The mechanism is over-generalization during candidate extraction, which can drop any directly stated fact. This applies to any session where a speaker directly answers a factual question and that fact must remain retrievable; it does not apply to indirect statements.
